research.searchCoverage: Bounded review on 2026-09-13 of official Beeminder API authentication and user/goal/datapoint reads, company identity (Beeminder, Inc., Portland, Oregon), Heartbleed 2014 operational write-up, and targeted incident/breach searches. Heartbleed was a historical OpenSSL exposure with same-day patch and next-morning restart; no confirmed unresolved Beeminder customer-data compromise was identified. Bounded coverage is not a breach-free claim.

Official Beeminder API v1 base URL https://www.beeminder.com/api/v1/, personal auth_token query authentication, GET /users/me.json, GET /users/{u}.json, GET /users/{u}/goals.json, GET /users/{u}/goals/{g}.json, and GET /users/{u}/goals/{g}/datapoints.json were confirmed on 2026-09-13. Beeminder, Inc. is a Portland, Oregon company. Heartbleed coverage from the 2014 Beeminder blog is recorded as a historical vulnerability exposure with remediation; no confirmed unresolved customer-data compromise was identified. Bounded coverage is not a breach-free claim.

incidents.finding: Beeminder documented Heartbleed exposure on Ubuntu, patched the same day the vulnerability was announced, and restarted the server the next morning after users reported it was still vulnerable. The post does not claim customer-data exfiltration; card data is described as handled by Stripe and never touching Beeminder servers.
incidents.remediation: OpenSSL patched the same day; server restarted the next morning.
incidents.limitation: Historical OpenSSL exposure; no confirmed unresolved Beeminder platform compromise in this bounded 2026-09-13 review.

research.waiverAuthority: User waiver dated 2026-09-13 permits historical non-China incident coverage.
